target: route "rbr-rounds": the round count of best-response restart and bidirectional improvement

findings.defect: The route's stated GAP is PROVABLY UNREACHABLE, and the route's explicit assertion that "no local, order-theoretic or monotonicity obstruction found in this round blocks the counter" is false: rbr:lem-constant, the very lemma the route offers as enabling the counter, combines with lem:switch to CAP the switches at each v_j at two, so the v_j cannot be counter bits and cannot recur as drivers.
findings.evidence: PROVED (aud:lem-twoswitch). Along any run of def:bsi (either variant), R_BR, or all-switches, C_max ⊆ S_sigma, so L_t := val_{sigma_t} is nondecreasing (lem:switch). Let v in Vmax have a successor c with L_t(c) constant in t (the GAP's b_j: "a constant gadget"), and let p be the other successor. Put P(t) := [L_t(p) > L_t(c)]; P is monotone nondecreasing because L_t(p) is nondecreasing and L_t(c) is constant. A switch of v TOWARDS c requires v in S_sigma with sigma_t(v)=p, i.e. NOT P(t); a switch AWAY from c requires P(t). Switches at v alternate in direction, and monotonicity of P forces every towards-c switch to precede every away-from-c switch; hence at most one of each, so sigma_t(v) changes at most TWICE over the entire run. Applied to the GAP shape (v_1..v_n the Max vertices, v_j -> (a_j,b_j), b_j constant): sigma changes at most 2n times in total, so L takes at most 2n+1 distinct vectors, so the sign of L(v_j) - L(Theta_j) reverses at most 2n times -- against the 2^{n-j} crossings the GAP demands, impossible for n >= 5. Independently: A <= 2n, so the route's OWN rbr:thm-track (dual form R <= k+(k+1)A) caps the strict run at n+(n+1)2n = O(n^2) rounds. Empirically corroborated: 1574 controlled vertices with a strategy-independent option, drawn from 400 random stopping games, both BSI variants, exact arithmetic -- 0 cases above 2 switches, and 0 violations of L-monotonicity (/tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-rbr/t_cap.py). The whole of next_steps (1) -- "graft SD(K)'s observer onto RD(n)'s cascade and make Theta_j read the lower bits" -- is therefore dead as written; the recurrence must come from controlled vertices BOTH of whose options are strategy-dependent (which is exactly what SD(K)'s observer v has and what RD(n)'s v_j lack).

findings.defect: The headline and the results entry assert "R = O(N 2^{min(m,k)}) -- BSI is polynomial whenever min(|Vmax|,|Vmin|) = O(log N)" for BSI. It is proved only for the STRICT variant. def:bsi's default rule is the VETO variant, for which the route's own remark identifies the failure mode and does not close it; the only support for the veto variant is 3000 random runs, which the standing rules declare to be no evidence.
findings.evidence: rbr:lem-greedy itself concedes the gap: in the veto variant Phi(sigma',U) = Phi(sigma,U) + |C^>_max| only, so U-tied vertices switch for free and the telescoping fails. rem:rbr-track then states the failure mode outright -- "on the tied set the veto is vacuous, so there def:bsi IS all-switches" -- and all-switches on m Max vertices can run for h*(m) >= 2^{m/2+1}-2 rounds by the document's own thm:blowup and cor:ceiling-general. So the honest veto-variant bound is R <= (B+1)*h*(m) + B = O(2^{m/2} 2^k), which is NOT O(N 2^{min(m,k)}) and is no better than the trivial A <= 2^m-1, B <= 2^k-1, R <= A+B = O(2^{max(m,k)}). My own sweep (1500 random stopping games, 6-11 non-sinks, both variants, exact arithmetic, t_track.py) found no violation and found runs attaining R = m+(m+1)B exactly -- but per the standing rule that is not evidence for the veto variant. Separately: the corollary has NO algorithmic content, because {min(m,k) = O(log N)} is trivially in P by enumerating the smaller player's 2^{min(m,k)} strategies and taking the componentwise min of val^tau (thm:eval-stopfree + determinacy); this is folklore (Condon 1992, from memory, unchecked). The content of rbr:thm-track is only the coupling A <= m(1+B), and that coupling is prop:bsi-oneplayer's greedy argument with w* replaced by a frozen guide -- which the route does acknowledge.

findings.defect: The paste-ready LaTeX asserts "all-switches takes 1 round, R_BR takes 2 (the best response is unique at each round)". The parenthetical is FALSE, and its falsity destroys the instance's role: with the other legitimate best response R_BR takes 1 round, exactly matching all-switches.
findings.evidence: Recomputed in exact arithmetic (t_small2.py). At round 0, sigma_0 = {3->1, 6->3, 7->4}, L = val_sigma has L(3) = L(9) = 0, so BOTH tau(4)=3 and tau(4)=9 satisfy profile_value(g,sigma_0,tau) = val_sigma, i.e. both are best responses (verified: is_BR=True for both). With tau(4)=3: S_sigma = [3,7], C_max = [3] (both variants) -> 2 rounds. With tau(4)=9: S_sigma = [3,7], C_max = [3,7] (both variants) -> 1 round. Since prop:bsi-br explicitly permits ANY best response, this 9-vertex instance is not a counterexample to "R_BR is never slower" in the rule's own worst-case sense. The route's SECOND instance (10 non-sinks) is correctly framed ("attained by a legitimate choice of best response"), and rbr:thm-readout is unaffected -- I verified by exhaustive recursion over EVERY best response at every round that RD(n) gives exactly n rounds for n = 2,3,4 in both variants (t_rdbr.py). Only the first instance's parenthetical must go.

findings.defect: Probable published prior art, in a stronger form, in a neighbouring model. From memory and UNCHECKED against the source: van Dijk, Loho and Maat, "The Worst-Case Complexity of Symmetric Strategy Improvement" (CSL 2024) proves an EXPONENTIAL lower bound for symmetric strategy improvement on parity / mean-payoff games -- the very rule the document identifies def:bsi with. If that is right, rbr:rem-attr's "we do not know of a published family separating either rule from all-switches" is wrong, and rbr:thm-readout's Theta(N) separation is a far weaker rediscovery.
findings.evidence: The route labels its attribution as from memory and unchecked, so by the round's rules this is not itself a defect -- but it is the single most important redirection the audit can offer. The document already records the van Dijk-Loho-Maat identification (rem:bsi-br, line 5912 of frontier.tex). If the exponential SSI lower bound exists, the route's GAP is very likely obtainable by transcribing that family through thm:stopping-transform rather than by hand-building a counter, and next_steps (1) should be replaced by that. The root agent should check this before integrating rbr:thm-readout as new.

verdict:
MEANS SOMETHING, BUT LESS THAN IT SAYS, AND ITS FORWARD PLAN IS DEAD.

1. IS IT NEW? Two results are genuinely new to this document and survive independent exact re-verification. rbr:thm-readout (RD(n): all-switches 1 round, R_BR n, BSI 2n, N = 9n) is the route's real contribution: it is the first family here on which the veto COSTS a factor Theta(N), and it is genuinely two-player and genuinely coupled (verified: reach(u_j) contains every v_i and u_i), which is what rem:bsi-gap demands. rbr:prop-sd (SD(K): one vertex switched K times, previous record 4) is new and correct. rbr:thm-track is new but small: rbr:lem-greedy is prop:bsi-oneplayer's greedy-count argument with w* replaced by a frozen guide -- the route says so -- and the only new content is that a Min round un-greedies at most m vertices, giving A <= m(1+B). NOT new / not worth it: rbr:prop-gain (four lines, |C| = 2, refutes nothing asserted), rbr:prop-slowlevel (SL(K) is a DISJOINT UNION of a Min cascade with its Max mirror, exactly the shape rem:bsi-gap already excludes -- verified by reachability), rbr:lem-constant (immediate from cor:comparison), rbr:prop-q16 (superseded by SD(K), as the route admits). Prior art the root agent must check before integrating: van Dijk-Loho-Maat, "The Worst-Case Complexity of Symmetric Strategy Improvement" (from memory, unchecked) very likely already gives an EXPONENTIAL lower bound for the same rule on parity/mean-payoff games; the route flags its attribution as unchecked, so this is not a defect, but if it holds then rbr:thm-readout is a much weaker rediscovery and the GAP is probably obtainable by transcription rather than by hand.

2. CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? No target-equivalent oracle is assumed and no barrier is claimed, so the usual traps are avoided. But two things are near-vacuous. (a) The corollary "BSI is polynomial whenever min(m,k) = O(log N)" has zero algorithmic content: that class is trivially in P by enumerating the smaller player's 2^{min(m,k)} strategies and taking the componentwise min of val^tau (thm:eval-stopfree + determinacy), folklore from Condon 1992 (memory, unchecked). And it is proved only for the STRICT variant; for def:bsi's default veto variant the route's own rem:rbr-track concedes the failure mode ("on the tied set the veto is vacuous, so there def:bsi IS all-switches"), and thm:blowup then permits h*(m) >= 2^{m/2+1}-2 rounds inside a single block. (b) rbr:lem-vacuous's leverage runs the wrong way: it conditions BSI hardness on realising a hard AUSO in a class strictly smaller than the one all-switches already fails in, so it makes the target harder; and the measured heights 1,2,3,4 at m = 1..4 (exactly m, against h*(m) = 1,2,4,7) are weak evidence the class is capped and worthless.

3. IS THE VERIFICATION HONEST? Mostly yes, and better than most rounds: every family is exact, every val is certified as a fixed point, and the route re-runs on fresh larger sizes. I independently reproduced RD(n) (n <= 8), SD(K) (K <= 10), GAIN(s), SL(K), the 9-vertex instance and its w*, from the graphs, with my own harness. Two honesty failures. (i) rbr:prop-small's first instance carries a FALSE parenthetical: the best response is NOT unique at round 0 (both tau(4)=3 and tau(4)=9 satisfy val_{sigma,tau} = val_sigma), and with the other one R_BR takes 1 round, matching all-switches -- so that instance is not a counterexample at all in the rule's own worst-case sense. (ii) The veto-variant half of rbr:thm-track rests on 3000 random runs, which the standing rule declares to be no evidence; my own 1500-game sweep also found nothing, which is equally no evidence.

4. THE REAL REMAINING GAP, stated more precisely than the route states it. The route's GAP is not merely open, it is REFUTABLE: because val_sigma is nondecreasing along every BSI/R_BR/all-switches run (lem:switch) and b_j is a constant gadget, each v_j switches AT MOST TWICE, so sigma changes at most 2n times, so val_sigma(v_j) and val_sigma(Theta_j) cross at most 2n times -- never 2^{n-j} -- and the strict run is capped at O(n^2) rounds by the route's own rbr:thm-track. The route's claim that "no local, order-theoretic or monotonicity obstruction found in this round blocks the counter" is false, and the obstruction is built out of the route's own two lemmas. The TRUE gap is: there is a stopping SSG family on N = poly(n) vertices and a pair start on which strict BSI performs superpolynomially many rounds, necessarily containing a controlled vertex BOTH of whose options are strategy-dependent that is switched superpolynomially often, and (by rbr:thm-track) with BOTH val_sigma and val^tau traversing superpolynomially long mutually endorsed improving runs. By rbr:thm-readout this neither implies nor is implied by the all-switches question, so it is a separate open problem of at least the same difficulty; every instance the route built has R <= |C| and both tracks of length at most |Vmax|, |Vmin|.

5. INTEGRATE? A TRIMMED version makes the paper BETTER; as submitted it makes it WORSE, because it would inject a false statement and a provably unreachable research direction into a document whose whole value is that its negative claims are exact.
INTEGRATE: rbr:def-rd + rbr:thm-readout (the route's one real result; add the van Dijk-Loho-Maat prior-art flag); rbr:def-sd + rbr:prop-sd + rbr:rem-sd, compressed, with the honest reading that K switches = K rounds and N = Theta(K^2); rbr:def-greedy + rbr:lem-greedy + rbr:thm-track, with "strict variant" carried into EVERY sentence including the min(m,k) corollary, the folklore triviality of that class noted, and the veto-variant case left as an explicit open item citing thm:blowup as the reason it may fail; rbr:prop-small's SECOND instance only (best-response dependence of R_BR's round count); and -- this is the item the route did not write -- the two-switch cap aud:lem-twoswitch as a corollary of lem:switch + rbr:lem-constant, together with its consequence that no counter whose bits have a strategy-independent option can exist.
DO NOT INTEGRATE: rbr:prop-gain; rbr:prop-slowlevel (decoupled union, already excluded by rem:bsi-gap); rbr:rem-psd (a search measurement of nothing, and prop:auso-size says no census can settle it); rbr:prop-q16 (superseded); rbr:prop-small's first instance; rbr:rem-gap in its current form -- replace it wholesale with the refutation and the true gap above.
CONDITIONAL: rbr:lem-vacuous only if bsr:prop-selfdual is integrated first, and only with the caveat that it raises the bar rather than lowering it.
